Among the many Apple Intelligence features coming to iOS 27, the Passwords app will get one particularly powerful capability: the ability to automatically change your passwords for you.

With Apple Intelligence, the Passwords app will be able to fix your leaked credentials for you on iOS 27

The new Apple Intelligence will be at the core of the upcoming iOS 27 and related software updates. One powerful new AI feature is directly related to the Apple Passwords app.

When Passwords launched two years ago, it already served as a dedicated hub for centrally managing login credentials, two-factor authentication codes, Wi-Fi passwords, passkeys, and more.

If any passwords in the database have problems, the app has always alerted you. For example, if your password is found in a data breach, or is reused across multiple accounts, the Passwords app will notify you.

However, until now, you still had to manually fix these problematic credentials yourself.

But Apple says that in iOS 27, their new agentic AI capabilities can change your passwords for you in many situations. According to the official website:

This feature lets you ensure that your login credentials are always secure and use sufficiently strong passwords, while minimising the actions and time required.

iOS 27 is currently in beta and is expected to roll out to all users in the coming weeks. The new Passwords feature is expected to debut in iOS 27.0, but its availability in the beta has been unstable, so it may be delayed until iOS 27.1.

Have you tried the new Passwords feature in the iOS 27 beta? How was your experience? Let us know in the comments.
